devices.name: Metonymy
devices.definition: Naming something by a word closely associated with it — cause for effect, container for contents, author for writings.

occurrences.note: "And the mountains shall be molten under him, and the valleys shall be cleft, as wax before the fire, and as the waters that are poured down a steep place." From a comparison with
"What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah? Are they not Jerusalem ? " i.e., Samaria and Jerusalem were the cause of the transgression of Israel
Licking the dust is put for defeat and submission
To pour water on the hands is put for serving

devices.name: Anaphora
devices.definition: The same word or phrase begins a run of successive clauses, hammering a theme.

devices.name: Anthropopatheia
devices.definition: Ascribing to God human feelings, parts, or actions, by way of condescension to us.

devices.name: Dialogismus
devices.definition: The speaker dramatises a dialogue, putting words into another's mouth.

devices.name: Personification
devices.definition: Giving human traits, action, or speech to something impersonal or abstract.

devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

devices.name: Polysyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions (“and … and …”) piled up to slow the pace and weight every item.

devices.name: Antonomasia
devices.definition: A proper name replaced by a descriptive title, or a title by a proper name (“the Son of man”).

devices.name: Ellipsis
devices.definition: A word or words deliberately left out, to be supplied by the reader — compression and force.

devices.name: Gnome (quotation)
devices.definition: A quotation or proverbial maxim woven in — a pithy saying cited for authority or point.

occurrences.note: reads (R.V.): " But thou Bethlehem Ephrathah, which art little to be among the thousands of Judah, out of thee shall One come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel."

devices.name: Hyperbole
devices.definition: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally, that drives a point home vividly.

devices.name: Parallelism
devices.definition: Successive lines echo one another in structure — saying the same thing twice, or balancing matched clauses.

devices.name: Paronomasia (wordplay)
devices.definition: A play on words that sound alike but differ in sense — pun, rhyme, near-repetition.

devices.name: Periphrasis
devices.definition: Circumlocution: a description put in place of the plain name of a thing.

occurrences.note: Here we have a double Periphrasis. "The doors of thy mouth," by Metonymy for words, or what is said, and " her that lieth in thy bosom " for thy wife

devices.name: Pleonasm
devices.definition: A deliberate redundancy — more words than strictly needed — to underline or solemnise.

occurrences.note: "And he shall stand and feed in the strength of the Lord, in the majesty of the name of the Lord his God "; i.e., in the majesty of Jehovah Himself

devices.name: Polyonymia
devices.definition: Heaping up several different names or titles for the same person or thing.

devices.name: Polyptoton
devices.definition: Repetition of the same root word in different inflections (“dying you shall die”).

occurrences.note: " A lamentation of lamentations," i.e., a great lamentation

devices.name: Rhetorical question
devices.definition: A question asked for effect, not for an answer — to affirm, deny, or provoke thought.

occurrences.note: " But the righteousness which is of faith, speaketh on this wise. Say not in thine heart. Who shall ascend into heaven ? "
